en.headline: Man injured in Morse Park football brawl; no arrests yet
en.dek: A 43-year-old man reported being attacked by about 11 people during an amateur match at the Wong Tai Sin pitch on Sunday evening; police classified the case as assault occasioning actual bodily harm.
body: Police are investigating a brawl that broke out during an amateur football match at Morse Park in Wong Tai Sin on Sunday after videos circulated online showing players exchanging punches and shoving near the goalmouth.

According to police, a 43-year-old man surnamed Chan reported that he was attacked by about 11 people at around 9.35pm. He sustained bruising to his left eye, a bleeding head wound and an abrasion to his left shoulder, and was taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital after treatment at the scene.

Footage circulating online showed a referee issuing red and yellow cards before the situation escalated into a mass confrontation, with players grappling on the ground despite attempts by others and the official to separate them. Police said no one had been arrested and classified the case as assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

zh.headline: 摩士公園足球賽變群毆 43歲男子受傷暫無人被捕
zh.dek: 黃大仙摩士公園周日晚業餘球賽發生衝突，43歲男子報稱遭約11人圍毆，左眼瘀傷、頭部流血，案件列襲擊致造成身體傷害。
body: 警方正調查黃大仙摩士公園周日晚一場業餘足球賽期間發生的衝突，網上片段顯示雙方球員在龍門前推撞及拳打腳踢。
警方表示，一名43歲姓陳男子報稱約晚上9時35分於球場疑遭約11人圍毆，左眼有瘀傷、頭部流血及左膊擦傷，經救護員包紮後送往伊利沙伯醫院治理。
網上片段可見球證先後出示紅牌及黃牌後場面失控，球員互相推撞扭作一團，球證及其他球員嘗試制止但未能即時分開雙方。警方將案件列為襲擊致造成身體傷害，暫未有人被捕。
